reply.answer: Most hyperscalers (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Oracle) currently depreciate servers over 5-6 years and networking equipment over similar or longer periods, having extended these useful lives in recent years (e.g., Amazon extended most servers to 6 years in 2024, Microsoft uses 6 years for servers, Google uses up to 6 years for servers and network equipment post-2023 revision). Neoclouds like CoreWeave, Nebius, and bitcoin miners-turned-AI-infra players (IREN, Applied Digital, Core Scientific, Cipher, TeraWulf) generally use shorter useful lives (4-6 years) given faster GPU obsolescence risk. If actual useful life were 3-4 years instead of 6, annual depreciation expense would roughly double for GPU-heavy capex, which would materially compress reported operating income and EPS for the hyperscalers and neoclouds—potentially cutting hyperscaler operating margins by several hundred basis points given depreciation is now often 15-20% of revenue. This would not directly affect cash flow or capex timing, but it would increase apparent capital intensity and lower ROIC/ROE optics, pressuring valuation multiples that assume long asset life. Companies with heavier leasing/colocation exposure (Digital Realty, Equinix, Iron Mountain, American Tower) are less directly exposed to this specific depreciation risk since they don't own the chips themselves.

claims.source: Amazon 10-K 2024 - extended useful life of servers to 6 years
Alphabet 10-K 2023 - extended servers/network equipment useful life to up to 6 years
Meta investor letters - servers depreciated over 5-5.5 years
CoreWeave filings - GPU useful life ~5-6 years
Core Scientific 10-K - miner/server useful life ~2-5 years
